thesis: Kimco Realty (NYSE: KIM) owns open-air shopping centers. Q3 2026 10-Q (full text downloaded; statements, FFO and same property NOI reconciliations, debt, equity and dividend notes read) filed 2026-10-29; 8-K 2026-10-29 listed and not read; an S-3 filed 2026-11-05 (shelf, not read). FFO available to common 936.6M for nine months versus 899.8M (+4.1%); diluted FFO per share 1.39 versus 1.33 (Q3 0.47 versus 0.44). Same property NOI 1,202.7M versus 1,163.9M (+3.3%; Q3 +4.9%), driven by minimum rent and lower credit losses. GAAP net income to common 575.6M versus 410.8M includes gains and a lower impairment base, so is not used. Price 25.62 (NYSE close 2026-11-11, two publishers); 664,489,869 common shares at 2026-10-21; market cap about 17.0B; annualized nine-month FFO 1.85 per share gives about 13.8x P/FFO (FFO yield about 7.2%); AFFO not computed. Dividend declared 0.28 per quarter (1.12 annual, 4.4% yield; 0.80 in nine months versus 0.75), about 60% of annualized FFO. Balance sheet 2026-09-30: notes payable 8,043.1M, mortgages 428.9M, cash 543.7M, preferred stock liquidation preference 483.5M, total liabilities 9,401.2M; June 2026 issuance of 600M 3.50% exchangeable senior notes due 2031. Operating cash flow nine months 978.0M (861.6M); improvements to operating real estate 273.9M and acquisitions 115.5M; dividends paid 560.1M, common buybacks 255.2M and preferred repurchase 73.9M, funded partly by 202.1M of JV distributions in excess of earnings (asset-level proceeds) and debt. Shares fell from about 675M weighted a year earlier to 666.5M in Q3.
counterthesis: Dividends paid, buybacks and redevelopment (about 1.09B for nine months including preferred repurchase and improvements) exceeded operating cash flow of 978M; the gap was bridged by JV distributions of 202M and a net rise in notes payable (7,719M to 8,043M) so buybacks are partly debt funded. Net debt to EBITDA, maturities, interest rate on refinancing, pro rata JV debt and recurring capital spending (AFFO) were not read, so true leverage and cash cover are unverified. Same property NOI growth is 3.3% for nine months, modest for 13.8x FFO; a rate spike or retail tenant bankruptcies would pressure both FFO and the multiple, and the 52 week high is 26.65 so the price is near its high. Exchangeable notes can dilute shares. Large index overlap (S&P 500 member): this would duplicate index fund exposure. Peers (Regency, Federal Realty, Brixmor, Simon) not compared and NAV and implied cap rate not estimated.
invalidation: Same property NOI growth below 2%, occupancy decline, net debt to EBITDA rising above about 5.5x, FFO per share flat while buybacks continue with debt, or refinancing at materially higher rates. Supportive: AFFO covering the dividend and buybacks without net debt growth.
